onboarding.title: Getting set up
onboarding.summary: This is the recommended first pass for new or returning users. Use the action buttons to jump into the real pages.

import.title: Import progress first
import.description: Use imports before touching manual setup. They are the fastest way to get most of your tracker into a usable state.

bullets.one: Import your Tarkov.dev profile first when you have it. That usually fills most of the account basics and tracked progress.
bullets.two: Import your EFT logs next. That can backfill quests and other progress with almost no manual clicking.
bullets.three: If both imports land cleanly, manual setup becomes a quick verification pass instead of rebuilding everything by hand.

profile.title: Finish the basics
profile.description: After imports, lock in the core profile fields and decide whether you want your progress synced to an account.

bullets.one: Set your game mode, edition, level, faction, and display name so filters and unlock requirements line up with your real account.
bullets.two: Signing in unlocks teams, API-backed features, and cloud storage so progress is easier to keep across devices.
bullets.three: If you are not ready to sign in yet, you can still track locally first and attach that progress to an account later.

tasks.title: Sanity-check tasks
tasks.description: The last high-impact cleanup step is task availability. Once that is accurate, the rest of the site becomes much more reliable.

bullets.one: On the tasks page, mark the quests you currently have available in-game for each trader. That backfills prerequisite chains much faster than manually completing old tasks one by one.
bullets.two: When something looks wrong, use the task card menu to report a data issue instead of forcing your tracker into a bad state.
bullets.three: After this pass, use the app-bar help button on any supported page to reopen the page guide or this onboarding flow.

dashboard.title: Dashboard guide
dashboard.summary: Use the dashboard to spot your best next step, review progress, and jump into the pages that need attention.
dashboard.hint: Get a quick overview of what the dashboard is showing and where to click next.

focus.title: Best next step
focus.description: The top card highlights the clearest immediate progress based on your current filters and tracked progress.
focus.bullet_one: Use it when you want one strong recommendation instead of browsing the full task list.
focus.bullet_two: If it looks wrong, check your task filters first because hidden tasks can change the recommendation.

progress.title: Progress cards
progress.description: The progress cards are shortcuts into tasks and needed items with your current totals already in context.
progress.bullet_one: Task and objective cards jump back into your quest list.
progress.bullet_two: Item cards jump straight to the matching needed-items view for tasks or hideout.

review.title: Longer-term review
review.description: Trader and milestone sections are for checking broader progression, not just your next click.
review.bullet_one: Use traders to see which quest lines still have the most work left.
review.bullet_two: Use milestones to check Kappa, Lightkeeper, and overall completion pace at a glance.

tasks.title: Tasks guide
tasks.summary: Use the tasks page to browse available work, switch perspectives, and narrow the list to exactly what you want to focus on.
tasks.hint: Get a quick explanation of task views, filters, and where the important settings live.

views.title: Pick a view
views.description: The top row changes how tasks are grouped so you can browse by list, trader, map, or graph.
views.bullet_one: List view is best for normal progression checks and quick search.
views.bullet_two: Trader, map, and graph views are better when you already know the angle you want to review.

filters.title: Trim the list
filters.description: Status filters let you focus on what is available now, locked, completed, or failed without leaving the page.
filters.bullet_one: Search works across task names and helps when the list feels too large.
filters.bullet_two: If a count looks lower than expected, one of the status or teammate filters is usually hiding results.

settings.title: Adjust behavior
settings.description: The cog opens display and filtering preferences that change how the task list behaves across sessions.
settings.bullet_one: Use settings when you want different default filters, team visibility, or map behavior.
settings.bullet_two: If the page feels off, settings are the first place to check before assuming data is missing.

needed_items.title: Needed items guide
needed_items.summary: Use needed items to combine task and hideout materials, then narrow the list to the exact items you still care about.
needed_items.hint: Get a quick explanation of the tabs, view modes, and the filters behind the cog.

scopes.title: Choose a scope
scopes.description: Tabs at the top switch between all items, task-only, hideout-only, and completed needs.
scopes.bullet_one: Use task-only when you are questing and do not want hideout materials mixed in.
scopes.bullet_two: Use completed when you want to review what you already satisfied instead of what is still missing.

views.title: Change the layout
views.description: List, grid, and combined views all show the same data but are optimized for different browsing styles.
views.bullet_one: List view is fastest for scanning counts and names.
views.bullet_two: Combined view groups repeated items together when you care more about totals than individual sources.

filters.title: Refine the list
filters.description: The settings drawer controls owned-item visibility, FIR rules, team needs, and other high-impact filters.
filters.bullet_one: If an item disappears unexpectedly, a drawer filter is usually the reason.
filters.bullet_two: Sorting by priority is best when you want the highest-impact items first.

hideout.title: Hideout guide
hideout.summary: Use the hideout page to see what stations are ready, what is blocked, and what materials still matter for upcoming upgrades.
hideout.hint: Get a quick explanation of hideout statuses, availability rules, and where to find the linked materials.

statuses.title: Read the statuses
statuses.description: The main filters split stations into all, available, locked, and maxed so you can focus on the right stage.
statuses.bullet_one: Available is the fastest way to see what you can build right now.
statuses.bullet_two: Locked is useful when you want to understand what requirements are still missing.

requirements.title: Control blockers
requirements.description: The settings menu can enforce station, skill, and trader requirements so availability matches how strict you want the page to be.
requirements.bullet_one: Turn requirement filters on when you only want upgrades that are fully buildable right now.
requirements.bullet_two: Turn them off when you want a broader planning view of what is coming soon.

materials.title: Follow the materials
materials.description: Each station card shows the items and prerequisites behind the next upgrade, with links back to the broader item workflow.
materials.bullet_one: Use station cards when you want upgrade details without leaving the page.
materials.bullet_two: Jump to needed items when you want the full cross-station shopping list for hideout progress.

tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.overview: TarkovTracker existe em dois domínios. TarkovTracker.io é o site original criado pelo fundador do projeto TarkovTracker e hospeda o código original. rg é a continuação ativamente mantida executada por um contribuidor de longa data e antigo mantenedor do projeto original, como um fork de código aberto gratuito sob a mesma licença GNU GPLv3. Este guia explica as diferenças e as formas apoiadas de refazer o seu progresso em TarkovTracker.org.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_1_title: Crie ou entre em sua conta TarkovTracker.org
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_1_desc: Crie uma conta TarkovTracker.org ou entre na conta onde você deseja acompanhar o seu progresso atual na limpeza.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_2_title: Importar metadados do seu perfil Tarkov.dev
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_2_desc: Abra as Configurações, escolha Importações e use a importação do perfil Tarkov.dev para restaurar os detalhes do perfil suportados, como nível, facção e habilidades.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_3_title: Importe seus logs de jogos EFT
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_3_desc: Na mesma guia Importações, selecione a sua pasta de logs EFT para recuperar os eventos de início e conclusão das missões que ainda estão presentes nos logs locais.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_4_desc: Verifique a sua lista de tarefas e esconda-se, e então restaure manualmente o progresso que Tarkov.dev e os seus logs de jogos disponíveis não puderam se recuperar.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.step_5_desc: Configure TarkovMonitor com um novo token de leitura TarkovTracker.org API para que futuras atualizações de progresso sejam suportadas para a sua conta .org.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_1_q: Qual é a diferença entre TarkovTracker.io e TarkovTracker.org?
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_1_a: TarkovTracker.io é o local original. É relativamente estável, mas já conhece questões e deixou de ser mantida - a sua última implantação foi em Agosto de 2024 e não existe qualquer desenvolvimento ou apoio activo. TarkovTracker. rg é o fork ativamente mantido: ele recebe atualizações regulares, suporta mudanças de jogo após EFT 0.15 e adiciona novas funcionalidades. Como está sob desenvolvimento ativo, pode ocasionalmente ter bugs ou tempo de inatividade, e, embora trabalhemos arduamente para a evitar, a perda de dados não pode ser excluída por completo.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_2_a: Use TarkovTracker.org. É a única versão que recebe atualizações, correções de bugs e suporte para Escape atual de conteúdo de Tarkov. As novas contas devem ser sempre criadas em TarkovTracker.org.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_3_q: Como faço para migrar meu progresso de .io para .org?
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_3_a: TarkovTracker.org não fornece uma importação direta de token .io. Crie ou entre no seu . conta rg, em seguida, use o perfil Tarkov.dev suportado e as importações de log EFT em configurações. Verifique as tarefas e oculte o progresso manualmente porque essas fontes não podem conter tudo registrado em .io. O progresso não sincroniza entre os dois sites.
tarkovtracker_org_vs_io.faq_4_a: Não. O domínio e implantação .io são de propriedade e controlados pelo fundador do projeto original. Não temos acesso a ele e não podemos corrigir, atualizar ou oferecer suporte para qualquer coisa no .io.

tarkovdev.overview: Tarkov.dev is the backbone of the community data ecosystem. It maintains an open-source dataset of items, quests, traders, hideout stations, and more, all accessible through free static JSON endpoints at json.tarkov.dev. TarkovTracker itself uses these endpoints to stay up to date with the latest game data. If you build tools, write guides, or just want to look up item stats, Tarkov.dev is the authoritative source.
tarkovdev.step_1_desc: Visit tarkov.dev to search items, check quest requirements, view trader inventories, and explore hideout station data in a clean, ad-free interface.
tarkovdev.step_2_desc: If you are a developer, point your HTTP client at json.tarkov.dev. The endpoint catalog is at json.tarkov.dev/endpoints. The API is free, requires no authentication for read queries, and returns static JSON files you can cache locally.
tarkovdev.step_3_desc: The Hideout Discord is the hub for data contributors, tool developers, and bug reports. If you spot outdated data or want to contribute, this is where it happens.
tarkovdev.tip_1: The JSON endpoints have no rate limit. For production apps, cache responses client-side to avoid redundant requests.
tarkovdev.tip_2: Tarkov.dev data updates frequently during wipe seasons. If something looks wrong, it may already be fixed in the latest dataset.
tarkovdev.faq_1_q: Is the Tarkov.dev API free to use?
tarkovdev.faq_1_a: Yes, the JSON endpoints are completely free for read queries. No API key or authentication is required for standard usage.
tarkovdev.faq_2_q: How often is the data updated?
tarkovdev.faq_2_a: Data is maintained by community contributors and updated as changes are discovered in-game. During active wipe periods, updates can happen multiple times per day.

tarkovmonitor.overview: TarkovMonitor is a desktop application by The Hideout team that watches Escape from Tarkov log files and can automatically mark completed quests in TarkovTracker. It also provides audio notifications, local statistics, and optional Tarkov.dev website integration.
tarkovmonitor.compatibility: Keep TarkovMonitor running while you play so it can watch new game log entries. It does not read game memory.
tarkovmonitor.step_1_desc: Download the latest Windows release ZIP from the official GitHub Releases page.
tarkovmonitor.step_2_desc: Extract the archive to a permanent folder, then run TarkovMonitor.exe. Do not run it directly from inside the ZIP file.
tarkovmonitor.step_3_desc: In TarkovMonitor settings, open the TarkovTracker integration section. Create a read-write API token in TarkovTracker Settings, then paste it into TarkovMonitor.
tarkovmonitor.step_4_desc: Play normally while TarkovMonitor stays open. When the game writes a supported quest-completion event to its logs, TarkovMonitor can mark that quest complete in TarkovTracker.
tarkovmonitor.troubleshooting_1_desc: Confirm the API token is read-write, has not expired, and that TarkovMonitor is running the latest release.
tarkovmonitor.troubleshooting_2_desc: Use Read Past Logs in Initial Setup, then choose the correct wipe and profile breakpoint.
tarkovmonitor.troubleshooting_3_desc: Match your TarkovTracker game mode setting to the mode you are playing, either PvP or PvE.
tarkovmonitor.tip_1: Generate a read-write API token in TarkovTracker settings. A read-only token cannot update progress.
tarkovmonitor.tip_2: Normal monitoring only processes new logs written while TarkovMonitor is running.
tarkovmonitor.faq_1_a: TarkovMonitor watches the log files that Escape from Tarkov writes locally. It does not read game memory, and the logs are not updated while a raid is in progress. Any third-party tool carries some risk, so use it at your own discretion.
tarkovmonitor.faq_2_q: Does TarkovMonitor work with PvE mode?
tarkovmonitor.faq_2_a: Yes. It supports both PvP and PvE. Match your TarkovTracker game mode setting to the mode you are playing.
tarkovmonitor.faq_3_q: Do I need TarkovMonitor to use TarkovTracker?
tarkovmonitor.faq_3_a: No. TarkovTracker works fully with manual input. TarkovMonitor only automates supported progress updates.

ratscanner.overview: RatScanner is an open-source desktop tool that identifies Escape from Tarkov items from screenshots and displays item data in an overlay. It operates externally and does not access game memory.
ratscanner.compatibility: Use borderless or windowed mode. Exclusive fullscreen may prevent the overlay from appearing.
ratscanner.step_1_desc: Download RatScanner.zip from the official GitHub Releases page. The project website may lag behind the latest release.
ratscanner.step_2_desc: Extract the ZIP to a permanent folder, then run RatScanner.exe. Do not launch it directly from inside the archive.
ratscanner.step_3_desc: Choose which item details appear in the overlay, set opacity, and confirm your scan hotkeys.
ratscanner.step_4_desc: Name scanning: open an item inspection window and click the magnifier. Icon scanning: hold the configured modifier key and left-click an item. RatScanner screenshots the item and displays its data.
ratscanner.troubleshooting_1_desc: Extract the full release folder first, then run the executable from that folder. If Windows or antivirus blocks it, confirm the file came from the official repository.
ratscanner.troubleshooting_2_desc: Make sure the item inspection UI is fully visible, then try name scanning from the magnifier or icon scanning with the configured modifier.
ratscanner.troubleshooting_3_desc: Switch Tarkov to borderless or windowed mode. Exclusive fullscreen often hides overlays.
ratscanner.troubleshooting_4_desc: RatScanner pulls market data from a third-party source, so values can lag behind live flea-market changes.
ratscanner.tip_1: Use settings to choose which item details appear and adjust overlay opacity.
ratscanner.tip_2: Displayed market values may lag behind live game or market changes.
ratscanner.faq_1_a: RatScanner reads item tooltips using screen capture and does not modify the game client or interact with game servers. Battlestate Games' stance on third-party tools can change, so use at your own risk.
ratscanner.faq_2_q: Does RatScanner work with the flea market?
ratscanner.faq_2_a: Yes. It shows current flea-market prices and can help compare flea versus trader value.
ratscanner.faq_3_q: Can RatScanner show items needed for TarkovTracker?
ratscanner.faq_3_a: It can show general item information from its data provider. For requirements based on your personal TarkovTracker progress, use the Needed Items page.
ratscanner.faq_4_a: Sim. Instale o RatScanner, abra a seção TarkovTracker em suas configurações e altere o backend TarkovTracker de .io para .org antes de entrar no seu tarkovtracker. token de API rg. A equipe TarkovTracker.org agora ajuda a manter o RatScanner, então integração e padrões da .org continuarão melhorando em versões futuras.

cultistcircle.overview: CultistCircle is a free community-built calculator for the Cultist Circle feature in Escape from Tarkov. It lets you look up recipes — what items you can sacrifice and what you get in return — without having to experiment in-game. Built by a solo community developer, it is a handy reference for planning your circle trades efficiently.
cultistcircle.step_1_desc: Go to cultistcircle.com to access the calculator. No account or download is required — it works entirely in your browser.
cultistcircle.step_2_desc: Use the search or browse functionality to find recipes by input item or output result. The calculator shows the trade ratios and possible outcomes for each combination.
cultistcircle.tip_1: Check the calculator before sacrificing rare items — some trades have much better value ratios than others.
cultistcircle.tip_2: Recipe data may lag behind game patches. If a recipe seems missing or incorrect, check back after the site has been updated.
cultistcircle.faq_1_a: Yes, CultistCircle is completely free and runs in your browser with no account required.
cultistcircle.faq_2_a: No, CultistCircle is an independent project by a solo community developer. It is listed here as a useful community resource.
